schema_version: v0 — skill-charter shape; migrates into the intention envelope when MAP.md Q6 lands
what: Frictionless capture of HISTORICAL or SHORT-TERM OPERATIONAL notes — what was true at a moment, kept because forgetting it would cost something soon. Writes a note record to CairnCommons/notes/.
why: Capture must be near-zero friction or thoughts are lost between the moment they surface and the moment there's time to act on them. A note is a holding pen — non-terminal, un-cast, un-proved — so it costs almost nothing to make and carries no false weight. It later gets picked up by /intent if it grows into work.
how_it_learns: Barely, and honestly so: /note is a thin capture utility; its only feedback is friction — notes that never get picked up signal format drag, so simplify. It accrues no gate-confidence of its own. Doesn't meaningfully learn, because thin. CORRECTED 2026-08-04, same day: this skill is not a cairn.machines.skill_block tenant, and the first version of this sentence concluded from that it was UNMEASURABLE. That was wrong, and wrong in the direction that matters — the firings were on disk the whole time, as records in CairnCommons/notes/. Not being a seam tenant means it is not JUDGED at a door; it never meant it was not counted. The count is 3 (see counted_by), and the disuse clause has had a number available to it since before it was written.
traces_to: Law 5 (a thought worth keeping gets an address)
the fluid-middle stance — non-terminal capture (learning-loop keystone)
owner: the skills charter gates writes; Akien ratifies changes (signature gate)

counted_by.address_in_words: CairnCommons/notes/*.json, records conforming to that store's declared template (v1 since 2026-08-10: text + date required, everything else optional)
counted_by.what_it_counts: records carrying the store template's required fields — text and date, which is what a /note firing produces. Measured 2026-08-04: 3 of 25 conform. RE-MEASURED 2026-08-10 under the RULED v1 template: 11 of 33. The other 22 are held design documents written straight into the store with arbitrary hand-authored shapes, and counting them as /note firings would be a count that is green for the wrong reason.
counted_by.THE_RED_THIS_MEASUREMENT_EXPOSED: RESOLVED 2026-08-10 by decisions/2026-08-10-a-note-is-prose-and-a-timestamp, and resolved in the direction this field did not expect. The store charter said 'the single commons emit chokepoint validates every record against the template below (Law 6)' and 22 of 25 records proved it did not. Akien's ruling: 'it just takes a note, there prolly doesn't need to be a workflow for it ... the schema would be {NOTE:prose_text} maybe with date time stamp'. So the defect was never a missing gate — it was an OVER-SPECIFIED TEMPLATE claiming an enforcement nobody wanted. The charter now declares no chokepoint, and Law 4 is satisfied by having no rule rather than an unenforced one. THE MEASUREMENT THAT SETTLES IT: the ruled template (text+date) selects EXACTLY the same 11 records as the old four-field one — the count was never wrong, only the charter's claim about a gate was.
counted_by.why_not_the_seam: the note record IS the firing artifact, and it is durable commons rather than instance-space — a better home than a berth that dies with the box. The 2026-08-10 ruling settles the fork this field named: the chokepoint red was fixed by CORRECTING THE CHARTER, not by enforcement and not by moving /note onto the seam, so this declaration STAYS. A seam door here would now contradict the ruling.
counted_by.the_number_is_the_disuse_clause: 3 firings at the baseline, and the narrowing that produced the clause happened the same day the count was first taken. So the clock on 'could wind up being excised through disuse' starts 2026-08-04 with a baseline of 3, and a disuse call made before that clock has run is a call made on no evidence. AT 2026-08-10 THE COUNT IS 11 — eight firings in six days, which is not disuse. And Akien's ruling reframes the clause: 'it's mostly for you', so the store's usefulness is measured by CC's use of it, not his.

proof: skill node → done only when cairnmap recompiles green (derivation gate). IOU until cairnmap exists — tracked in proofs/.
provenance: converged in the founding design conversation (MAP.md 'Workflow + starting skills', 2026-07-15) — 'anything in discussion not tracked elsewhere goes to notes'.
narrowed_2026_08_04: Akien, ruling the split when skill:/idea was built: 'slash note becomes more for historical or short term operational notes. could wind up being excised through disuse.' Before this, this charter's own why said a note 'later gets picked up by /intent if it grows into work' — which is now /idea's job, and /intent cites the idea in its from_idea field. What is left here is the short-half-life capture: the operational fact, the state of a thing at a moment. THE DISUSE CLAUSE IS NOT A DEPRECATION: this skill is not marked dying, it is marked COUNTABLE — and it can only be excised on measured disuse, never on an impression of it. A skill that is dying and a skill that was never wired look identical in an uncounted system.
